criteria.criterion: NASA's DART mission changed Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by at least 73 seconds
required_elements: NASA defined success as a change of 73 seconds or more in Dimorphos' orbit period
DART actually changed Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by at least 73 seconds
criteria.promise_scope: Actor: NASA. Beneficiary/subject: Dimorphos' orbit around its parent asteroid Didymos; no human beneficiary is specified. Location: Dimorphos orbit around Didymos in space. Benefit/action promised: DART would meet NASA's minimum success target if it changed Dimorphos' orbital period by 73 seconds or more.
criteria.observed_scope: Actor: NASA / the DART mission. Subject: Dimorphos' orbit around Didymos. Beneficiary: no human beneficiary specified. Location: space, specifically Dimorphos orbiting Didymos. Observed benefit/action: NASA reports and investigation-team findings that DART's impact altered Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by 32 minutes, later settling at 33 minutes and 15 seconds shorter than before impact.
criteria.explanation: The original success criterion was NASA's defined minimum orbit-period change of 73 seconds or more for Dimorphos. Observed outcomes directly report that DART's impact altered Dimorphos' orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, and later analysis says it settled at 33 minutes and 15 seconds shorter than before impact. Either observed change is far greater than 73 seconds, and it is for the same object and orbit specified in the original target. The sources therefore establish that NASA's DART mission met its minimum success target. The cited timing language only places the change after impact and during subsequent analysis; because the original undertaking did not set a separate delivery deadline, timing is not a limiting requirement here.

delivery_support.quote: Now, the investigation team has confirmed the spacecraft’s impact altered Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, shortening the 11 hour and 55-minute orbit to 11 hours and 23 minutes.

Over the following weeks, the asteroid’s orbital period continued to shorten as Dimorphos lost more rocky material to space, finally settling at 11 hours, 22 minutes, and 3 seconds per orbit – 33 minutes and 15 seconds less time than before impact.

criteria.fulfilled_part: NASA's DART mission changed Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by well over 73 seconds.

Requested scope: Did NASA's DART mission meet its target for changing how long Dimorphos takes to orbit Didymos?

NASA's DART mission changed Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by at least 73 seconds
Status: DELIVERED
The original success criterion was NASA's defined minimum orbit-period change of 73 seconds or more for Dimorphos. Observed outcomes directly report that DART's impact altered Dimorphos' orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, and later analysis says it settled at 33 minutes and 15 seconds shorter than before impact. Either observed change is far greater than 73 seconds, and it is for the same object and orbit specified in the original target. The sources therefore establish that NASA's DART mission met its minimum success target. The cited timing language only places the change after impact and during subsequent analysis; because the original undertaking did not set a separate delivery deadline, timing is not a limiting requirement here.

Benefit/action promised: DART would meet NASA's minimum success target if it changed Dimorphos' orbital period by 73 seconds or more.
Observed scope: Actor: NASA / the DART mission. Subject: Dimorphos' orbit around Didymos. Beneficiary: no human beneficiary specified. Location: space, specifically Dimorphos orbiting Didymos. Observed benefit/action: NASA reports and investigation-team findings that DART's impact altered Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by 32 minutes, later settling at 33 minutes and 15 seconds shorter than before impact.
Supported delivery: NASA's DART mission changed Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by well over 73 seconds.
Promise evidence: c1
Delivery evidence: c2, c3

Cited source excerpts (promise, delivery, or context as assessed above):
c1: “Before its encounter, NASA had defined a minimum successful orbit period change of Dimorphos as change of 73 seconds or more.”
https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-confirms-dart-mission-impact-changed-asteroids-motion-in-space/

c2: “Prior to DART’s impact, it took Dimorphos 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit its larger parent asteroid, Didymos. Since DART’s intentional collision with Dimorphos on Sept. 26, astronomers have been using telescopes on Earth to measure how much that time has changed. Now, the investigation team has confirmed the spacecraft’s impact altered Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, shortening the 11 hour and 55-minute orbit to 11 hours and 23 minutes. This measurement has a margin of uncertainty of approximately plus or minus 2 minutes.”
https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-confirms-dart-mission-impact-changed-asteroids-motion-in-space/

c3: “Over the following weeks, the asteroid’s orbital period continued to shorten as Dimorphos lost more rocky material to space, finally settling at 11 hours, 22 minutes, and 3 seconds per orbit – 33 minutes and 15 seconds less time than before impact. This calculation is accurate to within 1 1⁄2 seconds, Naidu said.”
https://www.nasa.gov/missions/dart/nasa-study-asteroids-orbit-shape-changed-after-dart-impact/?rand=772114

c4: “After further analysis, NASA confirmed that DART’s hypervelocity impact with Dimorphos successfully altered Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos, marking humanity’s first time purposely changing the motion of a celestial object and the first demonstration of asteroid deflection technology.”
https://science.nasa.gov/planetary-defense-dart/
